title: Sentinel sampling, acceptance matrix, and adaptive rollback response (Optimize)
creator: Evan Chen
description: Problem statement: Optimize needs a compact, unambiguous decision framework that ties promptset sampling, statistical acceptance criteria, and automated rollback triggers together. Current eval workstreams produce signal matrices (accuracy, hallucination rate, toxicity, latency) but lack a single canonical mapping from observed drift/regression to concrete rollout actions. This PRD defines: 1) a sentinel sampling plan for prompt cohorts that prioritizes high-value customers and long-tail intents, 2) per-signal statistical thresholds and minimum sample requirements for binary accept/reject decisions, 3) an adaptive rollback and mitigation ladder (canary slow-down, partial rollback, full rollback, mitigation-mode) with deterministic triggers, and 4) A/B gating rules for model upgrades in Optimize with clear stop/abort criteria. Goals: reduce manual triage by 60% when an eval detects regression, bound false-positive rollback rates to <2% per major release, and ensure noisy signals do not cause service-impacting rollbacks without cross-signal corroboration.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling: baseline promptset for each release must include: 10k IID production-like prompts (stratified across 8 cohorts: transactional, generative, summarization, instruction-following, low-resource languages, safety-edge, long-context, embeddings-use).

Minimum per-cohort sample size for actionability: 2500 prompts for top-4 cohorts, 800 prompts for secondary cohorts. If a cohort does not meet sample size, require pooled analysis and conservative decision rules.

Statistical tests: use two-sided bootstrap CI for nonparametric metrics and pooled t-test for continuous latency measures. Require p-value < 0.01 AND effect size >= 1.5 * baseline sigma to mark a strong regression signal.

Composite signal rule: a rollback candidate requires either (A) 1 strong regression in a high-priority signal (safety or hallucination) OR (B) >=2 moderate regressions across distinct signals (accuracy drop >= 1.5% absolute and latency increase >= 10ms) in the primary cohorts.

False-positive guardrail: require at least 3 independent daily runs with consistent signal direction before triggering automated partial rollback, unless customer-facing severity threshold exceeded (see triggers).

A/B traffic ramp: Start at 1% traffic for the candidate model, progress to 5% after 12h if no stop conditions, 25% after 48h, 50% after 96h, and full rollout only after 7 days with continuous monitoring passing all canary checks.

Stop/rollback triggers during A/B: immediate abort if safety metric increases >0.5% absolute OR hallucination rate doubles compared to control; partial rollback (revert to 10% exposure) if composite signal rule met; full rollback if composite signal persists for 3 consecutive daily runs.
Operational SLO effect caps: ensure latency P95 increase across all routes is <= 7% or <= 30ms (whichever is smaller) during canary for proceeding to next ramp step.

Alerting and human-in-the-loop: any safety-flagged regression auto-pages on-call SRE and ML lead and stalls ramp; automation may proceed only after documented triage and explicit approval with root-cause hypothesis logged.

Reporting: each candidate rollout must produce a release-eval artifact (linkable JSON + dashboard) that includes cohort-level metrics, CIs, sample counts, and the decision verdict. Artifacts must be retained for 90 days.
notes: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting held. Attendees: Aisha (PM), Nikhil Rao (ML), Priya Sen (SRE), Rahul Gupta (Data Eng). Agreed to prioritize safety and hallucination signals when weighing rollbacks.

2026-02-20: Spike by ENG (ENG-19832) exploring bootstrap CI runtime and required sample throughput. Outcome: nightly eval runs will be retained; online incremental bootstrap pipeline scoped as follow-up.

2026-02-28: Design feedback from Design (DES-2107) requested clarification on how to present 'partial rollback' states in the Console. Action: add explicit UX states (paused, degraded, mitigated) in console-2026.03.
2026-03-05: PM decision: require both statistical significance (p<0.01) AND practical effect-size threshold to reduce churn from noisy signals. Rationale documented in linked PRD.

2026-03-10: Scoped down initial automation: MVP automates detection and alerting; automated partial rollback gated behind canary confirmation (3 runs) and explicit ML lead opt-in. Full automation deferred to next cycle.
2026-03-12: Updated acceptance criteria to require at least 3 independent daily runs for automated partial rollback to limit false positives (see acceptance_criteria entry).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): implement sentinel sampling scaffolding, nightly eval runs, composite-signal detector, alerting to on-call. Timeline: 4 weeks.
Phase 2: A/B gating automation with traffic ramps and stop conditions wired to rollout controller. Timeline: next cycle (6 weeks after Phase 1).
Phase 3: Full automation of adaptive rollback ladder with policy templating for enterprise customers (including per-customer thresholds). Timeline: 2 cycles after Phase 2.
risks: Noisy signals causing unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by requiring p<0.01 + effect size and 3-run corroboration.
Insufficient prompt coverage for niche cohorts — mitigated via pooled analysis and explicit sampling quotas in release checklist.
Automation performing rollback without human oversight for enterprise customers — mitigated: default to human-in-the-loop; enterprise can enable opt-in automation later.
